items.english: Taki had grown heavy with thinking of nothing but his creative work, his novel, so with his sketch box in hand he went out for a walk. — Down the stone steps, then on wavering down toward the sea, halfway through the pine wood near the shore. More troubled by passersby than by the view, he left the little path and, stooping, hid himself among the dwarf pines that caught at his head. Then, coming to the broken edge of the hill, he sat cross-legged among the evening primroses. Far off, on the sand that shone grey, four or five things like cloth wrappers toyed with by the wind were solemnly circling, and wondering what they could be he looked up and found them the shadows of gulls wheeling low in great rings.
notes: I kept the cloth wrapper for the wrapping cloth simile and kept the circling things as the gulls' shadows, as the Japanese has it.

items.english: On the hot evening of the second day he finished his board of the distant sea, yet Taki came trudging blankly home and near the foot of the stone steps met his wife, who seemed to have been loitering there looking for him.
notes: Second day is left vague in the Japanese; I kept it literal.

items.english: "Just got here? Have you come to visit?"
"I've come to watch them catch the carp, but they say they just can't catch them!"
notes: I keep catch throughout for tsukamaeru as the story's fixed verb.

items.english: "Again... They had better give it up. To begin with, carried to a pond like that they would make no show at all, they would only strike the nose pitifully—"
"But wasn't it dug on purpose for that? It is small but they say it is fairly deep, so it will be all right!"
"They say that hole was dug because earth was wanted somewhere and there was no help for it. — It seems there are a few goldfish and worthless carp in it, but I think that is just right."
notes: I kept hole against pond to hold the contrast Taki is making.

data.say: Drafted the opening walk and first pond exchange, holding catch and pond language steady.
